---
title: "Steering and headset"
---

Headset adjustment ("steering play") and related notes from personal
maintenance logs.

## Threaded headset adjustment {#sec-headset}

Excess play is felt as a knock or looseness when rocking the bike with
the front brake on.

Reference video: [headset adjustment](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ca2cVrr7l-U)

### Adjustment sequence

1. Loosen the **locknut** (top nut).
2. Turn the **adjusting cup / bearing race** until play just disappears
   with the fork centred — the bars should turn smoothly without binding.
3. Hold the adjusting cup in place and re-tighten the **locknut**.
4. Re-check: no play, no notchiness.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-headset-adjust
%%| fig-cap: "Threaded headset adjustment protocol."
flowchart TD
  A[Front brake on — rock bike] --> B{Play at headset?}
  B -->|No| C[OK — check periodically]
  B -->|Yes| D[Loosen locknut]
  D --> E[Turn adjusting cup to remove play]
  E --> F[Bars swing freely?]
  F -->|No — tight| G[Back off adjusting cup slightly]
  F -->|Yes| H[Hold cup — tighten locknut]
  G --> E
  H --> I[Re-test for play]
  I --> B
```

## Integrated / threadless headsets {#sec-headset-threadless}

Most modern road bikes use a threadless system:

1. Loosen stem clamp bolts.
2. Turn the **top cap** bolt (usually 4 or 5 mm hex) to remove play —
   typically **0.2–0.5 Nm** preload, just enough to seat the bearings.
3. Align the stem with the front wheel.
4. Torque stem clamp bolts evenly to manufacturer spec.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-threadless-headset
%%| fig-cap: "Threadless headset adjustment."
flowchart LR
  A[Loosen stem clamps] --> B[Tighten top cap to remove play]
  B --> C[Align stem]
  C --> D[Torque stem bolts to spec]
  D --> E[Check bearing feel]
```

## Symptoms and causes {#sec-headset-symptoms}

| Symptom | Likely cause |
| --- | --- |
| Knock when braking | Headset too loose |
| Notchy steering | Corroded or pitted bearings |
| Bars cannot centre | Bent fork or misaligned stem |
| Play returns quickly | Locknut not secured; wrong washer order |

## Related: pedal and crank orientation {#sec-steering-related}

Pedal thread directions and crank removal are covered in
[bike overview](bike-overview.qmd#sec-pedals) and
[gears](gears.qmd#sec-gears-chainrings). Always remove pedals before
extracting cranks so the threads are not damaged by leverage on the
levers.
